articles.headline: Experts body calls for urgent, focused efforts against measles in WHO South-East Asia
articles.headlineJa: 専門家団体、WHO東南アジアで麻疹に対する緊急かつ集中的な取り組みを呼びかけ
articles.summary: An independent regional expert body has called for urgent and targeted action to close immunity gaps and strengthen surveillance at sub-national level, as countries in the WHO South-East Asia Region report outbreaks and increase in measles cases.
articles.summaryOriginal: An independent regional expert body has called for urgent and targeted action to close immunity gaps and strengthen surveillance at sub-national level, as countries in the WHO South-East Asia Region report outbreaks and increase in measles cases.
articles.summaryJa: WHO東南アジア地域の国々が麻疹の流行と症例の増加を報告している中、独立した地域専門家団体は、免疫力のギャップを埋め、準国家レベルでの監視を強化するための緊急かつ的を絞った行動を呼びかけた。

articles.headline: WHO South-East Asia Regional Verification Commission reviews progress towards measles and rubella elimination
articles.headlineJa: WHO東南アジア地域検証委員会、麻疹・風疹撲滅に向けた進捗状況を検証
articles.summary: Colombo, Sri Lanka, 22 June 2026— The 11th Meeting of the WHO South-East Asia Regional Verification Commission for Measles and Rubella Elimination opened today in Colombo, Sri Lanka, bringing together members of the Regional Verification Commission and chairs of National Verification Committees from all 10 countries of the WHO South-East Asia Region.
articles.summaryOriginal: Colombo, Sri Lanka, 22 June 2026— The 11th Meeting of the WHO South-East Asia Regional Verification Commission for Measles and Rubella Elimination opened today in Colombo, Sri Lanka, bringing together members of the Regional Verification Commission and chairs of National Verification Committees from all 10 countries of the WHO South-East Asia Region.
articles.summaryJa: コロンボ、スリランカ、2026年6月22日—麻疹・風疹撲滅のためのWHO東南アジア地域検証委員会の第11回会議が本日スリランカのコロンボで開幕し、WHO東南アジア地域の10カ国すべてから地域検証委員会のメンバーと国家検証委員会の委員長が一堂に会した。

articles.headline: From Invisible to Immunized: How TrackVac Is finding India’s most missed children
articles.headlineJa: 目に見えないところから予防接種を受ける人へ: TrackVac はインドで最も行方不明の子供たちをどのように見つけているのか
articles.summary: Across 143 Gavi‑supported districts in 11 states of India, thousands of children remain unseen by the immunization system each year. These are “zero‑dose” children—those who have not received even a first dose of the pentavalent vaccine before their first birthday—or children who were identified once but subsequently missed. While monitoring mechanisms existed, the absence of a standardized follow‑up system meant that identification did not consistently translate into vaccination. For many children, being missed once meant remaining missed.

articles.summaryJa: インドの 11 州の 143 の Gavi 支援地区では、毎年数千人の子どもたちが予防接種制度を受けられずにいます。これらは「ゼロ投与」の子供たち、つまり1歳の誕生日までに5価ワクチンの初回投与さえ受けていない子供たち、または一度は特定されたものの、その後見逃された子供たちだ。監視メカニズムは存在していましたが、標準化された追跡システムがないため、識別が一貫してワクチン接種に結びつかないことを意味していました。多くの子どもたちにとって、一度寂しくなることは、そのまま寂しくなることを意味します。

articles.headline: Reaching every child in India’s expanding cities: Urban immunization through partnerships and WHO frameworks
articles.headlineJa: 拡大するインドの都市のすべての子どもたちに届ける：パートナーシップとWHOの枠組みを通じた都市部の予防接種
articles.summary: Rapid urbanization presents one of the most complex challenges for immunization programmes. In Gautam Budh Nagar district of Uttar Pradesh—part of India’s fast‑growing National Capital Region—population mobility, informal settlements, and fragmented urban services have made it difficult to identify and reach every eligible child. Migrant families and residents of slum and peri‑urban areas are especially vulnerable to being missed by routine immunization systems.

articles.summaryJa: 急速な都市化は、予防接種プログラムにとって最も複雑な課題の 1 つをもたらします。インドの急速に成長する首都圏の一部であるウッタル・プラデーシュ州のゴータム・ブッダ・ナガル地区では、人口の流動性、非公式居住地、細分化された都市サービスにより、対象となるすべての子どもを特定して支援することが困難になっています。移民家族やスラム街や都市近郊地域の住民は、定期的な予防接種制度が受けられない可能性が特に高くなります。

articles.headline: Measles–Rubella vaccination drives boost immunization coverage in Andhra Pradesh, India
articles.headlineJa: 麻疹風疹ワクチン接種により、インドのアーンドラプラデーシュ州での予防接種率が向上
articles.summary: Between January and March 2025, seven measles outbreaks were reported in Andhra Pradesh—six in Alluri Sitarama Raju district and one in Vizianagaram district. Root cause analysis identified immunity gaps resulting from missed and dropout children, as well as weaknesses in routine immunization (RI) microplanning, particularly in urban, peri‑urban, border, tribal, and other high‑risk areas.
